title: rhino-core: plan-and-grill, verify and pr-story
bridge: The three core skills are like the team's PR checklist, split by moment: before code, before done, and when opening the PR. Except: the reader is an agent as well as a person. So each skill says when it applies, gives goals and reasons instead of commands, and is tested by eval cases.
intro: rhino-core is the plugin every engineer and every agent gets. Its first three skills carry the habits the platform depends on. Agree the checks before code, and prove them before done. Then tell the story in a PR that a reviewer from the other team can read. This lesson walks through each SKILL.md line by line.

picture.caption: One ticket, three moments, three skills; Nova and people use the same ones.

nodes.label: verify: checks run, a bug planted, proof

steps.text: big or vague? ask first; small and clear? plan now
a one-screen plan with 3-5 checks and their proof
approves the plan; the work starts

sections.h: What a core skill looks like
p: Each skill is plugins/rhino-core/skills/<name>/SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and a short body. Its name must match the folder; its description says what it does, starting with when to use it. when_to_use lists the moments that should load it. Claude reads these two fields to decide whether to load the skill, and plugin CI limits their length (lesson g8-3).

The body follows STYLE.md (lesson g8-1): a goal, reasons, signs to look deeper, calm words. Depth goes into references/ files that load only when needed. Every skill ships with 3 to 10 eval cases in the plugin's evals/ folder.

The three skills also have to match G4. Nova's readiness check and grill step use plan-and-grill and post the same plan format on Jira and Slack. Nova's PR judge reads descriptions written with pr-story.

callout.text: Most rework starts with a misread ticket, and most review time goes into guessing whether a change was checked. These three skills target those two costs, for people and for Nova alike.

p: Before code, the skill decides one thing: ask the requester questions first, or write the plan now. Then it writes a one-screen plan. To grill means to ask the requester sharp questions before you build. Create plugins/rhino-core/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and this file.
sections.because: We tell the agent when to ask first, because a question on a vague ticket is cheaper than a second PR.

code.text:
---
name: plan-and-grill
description: "Use before writing code for a ticket or task: decide whether to ask the requester questions first, then write a one-screen plan with the definition of done, 3-5 checks including an edge case, the proof each check needs, an estimate, risks and what is out of scope."
when_to_use: "A Jira ticket, bug report or feature request is about to be built; the user says 'plan this' or 'grill me'; the task is big or vague."
argument-hint: "[Jira key or task description]"
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---
# plan-and-grill

Goal: agree what "done" means before any code, so the work is checked against the ask, not against itself.

## Ask first, or plan now?
Ask the requester first when the ticket is big, spans teams, or two readings would lead to different code. Signs:
no example, a vague verb ("improve", "support"), a screen with no states, a change to an API others use. A small,
clear fix (a typo, copy, one obvious bug) goes straight to the plan. For big tasks read references/grill-questions.md.

## The plan (one screen)
1. Done means: 1-2 sentences in the user's words.
2. Checks: 3-5, at least one edge case. Each says what it looks at (what the user sees, an API response, a row
   count) and its proof: a short video, screenshots at 760 and 1440, or text output.
3. Screen states for UI: empty, loading, error, long content.
4. Estimate, risks, and what is out of scope.

sections.h: Teaching plan-and-grill with examples and evals
p: The body above is the core. Around it, write goals, reasons, examples and signs to look for. Say when a small clear fix skips the grill, and that a good check looks at what the user sees. Add one worked example each for an FE and a BE ticket.

references/grill-questions.md holds the questions for big or vague tasks, so they load only then. Three eval cases prove the skill helps. A vague ticket gets questions before a plan. A typo fix gets a plan and no grill. The plan names an edge case and the proof for each check.

verify is the skill for any code change before saying done. It runs the area's verify command (lesson g7-5) and looks at what the user sees. Then it plants a bug to prove a check can fail, and records proof.
Until G7's commands land, references/per-area.md lists the old ones. For FE: npm run lint, npm run check-types and vitest on related files. For BE: scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh.
sections.because: We start from the area's verify command, because it is the same command the Stop hook and CI run.

code.text:
---
name: verify
description: "Use before saying a code change is done: choose checks that prove it works, run the area's verify command, show a new check can fail by planting a bug, and record proof a reviewer can see."
when_to_use: "After editing code, tests or config; when a check fails and you need to know whether it's yours; when filling in 'How it was checked' in a PR."
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---
# verify: proof, not claims

## Where to start
Run the area's verify command (references/per-area.md): `npm run verify` in frontend/, `poe verify` for cloud,
client and sdk. Then check what the user would see: open the flow in FCP Lab with seed data (fcp-lab skill), or
call the API and read the response.

## Signs to look deeper
You changed a serializer, a migration, a proto, a public SDK function or shared UI; there is no test near the
diff; the change is about timing, permissions or time zones.

sections.h: verify, part 2: plant a bug, own the failure, record proof
p: Planting a bug means flipping one condition or return value in your change, running the check, watching it fail, and reverting. If the check still passes, it does not cover your change. That is how a reviewer knows the check could have failed.

A failing check is yours until main's latest run shows the same failure; then link that run. The answer is to fix the code. Do not skip, delete or loosen a check; if you think a test is wrong, say so in the PR. Proof is a video up to 30 seconds for flows, screenshots at 760 and 1440 for layout, or text output. Use seed data only.
sections.because: We make the agent prove a check can fail, because a check that passes on broken code proves nothing.

code.text:
## Prove a check can fail
Plant a small bug in your change (flip a condition), run the check, watch it fail, revert. If it still passes,
the check doesn't cover your change: write a better one.

## When a check fails
It's yours until main's latest run shows the same failure; then link that run and say so. The answer is to fix
the code, not to skip, delete or loosen the check. If you think a test is wrong, explain why in the PR and leave
the call to the reviewer.

## Record the proof
Per check: the command, pass or fail, and the proof the plan named (a video up to 30 s, screenshots at 760 and
1440, or text). Seed data only.

notes.text: The planted-bug habit.
Flip a condition, run, watch it fail, revert.
If it still passes, the check does not cover the change.
Who owns a red check.
Yours, unless main already fails the same way; then link the run.
Fix the code, not the check.
Disagree in words; the reviewer decides.
What to write down per check.
The command, pass or fail, and the proof the plan named, labelled by check.
Never real data in proof.

callout.text: Point frontend/AGENTS.md and the root CLAUDE.md at it with one line: use the verify skill (rhino-core) before you say done. Write four eval cases. A frontend edit gets FE commands. A new test gets a planted bug. It will not delete a failing test. It links main's run when a failure is not ours.

p: Anyone may review any area, so every PR must be readable by someone from the other team in a few minutes. pr-story writes the description with fixed headings in a fixed order. One template for people and agents means reviewers always know where to look.
sections.because: We fix the title format and a word budget, because a reviewer decides in the first screen whether they understand the PR.

code.text:
---
name: pr-story
description: "Use when opening or updating a pull request or posting a Jira ticket update: writes the description with our fixed headings, in plain words for a reviewer from the other team, with the right proof (video, screenshots, a diagram, text, or nothing)."
when_to_use: "gh pr create, gh pr edit, a draft PR becoming ready, or a status comment on a ticket."
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---
# pr-story

A reviewer from the other team should understand this PR in two minutes. Same headings, same order, every time.
Keep the part above the fold under about 300 words; link long output instead of pasting it.

Title: `[FE] RH-1234: what changes for the user` (`[BE]` for backend).

notes.text: The skill's name.
When opening or updating a PR or posting a Jira update: fixed headings, plain words, the right proof.
gh pr create, gh pr edit, a draft becoming ready, a ticket status comment.
The body starts with the reader.
The goal: understood in two minutes, same headings every time.
A budget above the fold; link long output instead of pasting it.
[FE] or [BE], the ticket key, and what changes for the user, like this repo's commits.

sections.h: pr-story, part 2: the headings, and fcp's template
p: fcp's existing template moves to the same headings instead of a second template being added. In .github/pull_request_template.md, Summary of Changes becomes What changes, and References becomes Why. Testing Performed becomes How it was checked plus What was not checked. Implementation Details becomes Where to look first. Add Risk and rollback and the folded details block.

references/media.md says which proof fits. Flows get a video up to 30 seconds, and layout gets before and after screenshots at 760 and 1440. A changed flow between services gets a diagram, API calls and migrations get text, refactors get nothing. A ticket comment gets status, PR link, what was found, and before and after media for visual changes.
sections.because: We put the checks right after Why, because a reviewer's first question is whether the change was proven.

code.text:
## What changes
1-3 plain sentences about the visible effect.
## Why
The ticket link, and the root cause in one line with file:line.
## How it was checked
Each check from the plan: pass or fail, with its proof labelled by check.
## What was not checked, and why
## Risk and rollback
The risk, how to revert, what to watch after merge.
## Where to look first
2-3 files, and any question for the reviewer.
<details><summary>Receipt, trace and cost</summary>Self-review receipt, trace link, harness suggestions, cost and time.</details>

Pick media with references/media.md. Never pictures of code or logs, never real data.

quiz.q: A ticket says "Fix the typo on the login button". What does plan-and-grill do?

options.text: Asks the requester three grill questions first.
options.why: A small, clear fix goes straight to the plan.

options.text: Writes a short plan with checks, and no grill.
options.why: Questions are for big tasks, cross-team work or tickets with two readings.

options.text: Skips the plan, because the change is one line.
options.why: Every change gets a plan; a typo gets a short one.

quiz.q: Nova's new test passes. How does verify say Nova should prove the test is useful?

options.text: Run it three times to show it is stable.
options.why: Stability is not the question; whether it can fail is.

options.text: Plant a bug in the change, see the test fail, revert, and note what was planted.
options.why: A check that cannot fail on broken code proves nothing.

options.text: Ask the reviewer to run it locally.
options.why: The proof belongs in the PR, recorded by the author.

quiz.q: A test fails and main's latest run fails the same way. What does verify say?

options.text: Link main's run and say the failure is not ours.
options.why: It is yours until main shows the same failure; then you link it.

options.text: Skip the test in this PR, since main is red anyway.
options.why: Never skip, delete or loosen a check.

options.text: Fix main's failure in this PR first.
options.why: That widens the PR; linking the run is enough.
